result:
**Not ready to publish.** One claim has to change.

**Claims check**

| Claim | Status |
|---|---|
| Chamomile and Lemon Balm | Product fact, fine |
| "gentle, honeyed" | Flavour description, fine |
| "caffeine-free" | Ingredient fact, fine |
| "to help you wind down and sleep better" | **Unsupported.** Health claim |
| "Certified organic by the Soil Association" | Allowlisted, exact wording |
| "20 plastic-free tea bags" | Count is a product fact. "Plastic-free" is allowlisted |

**Problem**

"Sleep better" is a health claim, and the policy bans health claims of any kind. "Help you wind down" is softer, but it still implies a relaxation benefit, so I'd cut the whole benefit phrase rather than keep half of it. There is also a likely platform and regulatory risk with sleep claims on a food product.

**Compliant version**

> Chamomile and Lemon Balm. A gentle, honeyed, caffeine-free blend, easy to drink in the evening. Certified organic by the Soil Association. 20 plastic-free tea bags.

"Easy to drink in the evening" is a serving suggestion, not a benefit claim. If you'd rather not suggest a time of day, "A gentle, honeyed, caffeine-free blend" works on its own.

Everything else passes: no banned words, no superlatives, no invented numbers, no urgency, UK spelling. A product page on our own site needs no disclosure label. Sam still needs to approve the final copy.

```json
{"issues": [{"quote": "to help you wind down and sleep better", "type": "health_claim"}], "publish": false}
```
